title: The four pillars policy on bank mergers
summary: Successive governments have ruled out mergers between the four major banks. The policy is not in any law; it would be applied through the Treasurer's approval powers under the Banking Act 1959 and the Financial Sector (Shareholdings) Act 1998. The Productivity Commission found in 2018 that it is a 'redundant convention'.

instruments.title: Four pillars policy (government policy, not legislated)
Banking Act 1959
instruments.provisions: Treasurer's approval of transfers and amalgamations of banking business

direction_rationale: The Productivity Commission found 'no evidence that the Four Pillars policy has enhanced competition; and far more reasons to conclude that it may have dissuaded it by embedding a fixed market structure', and that removing the threat of takeover among the majors dulls their incentive to perform.

verified.notes: A policy, not a law: no dates. Quotes are from finding 6.2 and box 6.4 of the Productivity Commission's 2018 report, read in full.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 28 October 2026 (phase 4, second tranche, of the productivity framework pivot) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify the description, industries and assessment before use.

assessment.summary: A ban on mergers among the four major banks. Competition law and the Treasurer's approval powers already allow such a merger to be blocked; the Productivity Commission found the policy protects a fixed market structure and removes the takeover threat that would otherwise discipline the majors.

marks.reason: Shields the major banks from takeover by each other and locks in a four-bank structure (Productivity Commission, 2018).

assessment.confidence_note: The Productivity Commission judged that other prudential and regulatory settings reduce competition far more; the policy's own effect is likely small and could be positive if it prevents a merger that competition law would allow.

responsible.note: Administers the Banking Act 1959 and the Financial Sector (Shareholdings) Act 1998.
